subject: Distribution of a neuron across each neuropil

messages.author: e34bfd7e52d24c65
messages.subject: Distribution of a neuron across each neuropil
parts:
Hi natverse team,

I was hoping to use your powerful suite of R packages to analyze the data released by FlyCircuit, and would greatly appreciate any help with regards to a few questions that I have.

1. I was wondering why the template flybrain (e.g., plot3d(FCWP)) looks squished front-to-back? Are the coordinates not isometric? I want to make sure that I am not doing something wrong.

2. Given a FlyCircuit neuron, I want its distribution across each neuropil region (FCWBNP.surf$RegionList), i.e., the overlapping voxel count of the neuron per neuropil region. This voxel count is provided for 16129 neurons in the dataset http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/flycircuit/dpscanon.rds, but how can I calculate this for a new (not included in the dataset) neuron scraped from the FlyCircuit website?

While the voxel counts would be ideal, I suspect it would also be sufficient for my purposes to instead just get a distribution of the segment lengths (of the neuron) in each neuropil region. Below is the sequence of steps that I have been able to successfully implement so far:
  • fc_read_neurons() - to scrape a neuron from the FlyCircuit website.
  • xform_brain() - to register the neuron into FCWP space.
  • prune_in_volume() - to obtain a break-up of the number of vertices and segments present in each neuropil region.
However, I am unsure of how to proceed next. How can I calculate the segment lengths, and ultimately determine what proportion of the neuron is present in each neuropil?

Thank you for your help.

Ketan Mehta, PhD

parts:
Dear Ketan,

Thanks for your interest in the natverse.
> 1. I was wondering why the template flybrain (e.g., plot3d(FCWP)) looks squished front-to-back? Are the coordinates not isometric? I want to make sure that I am not doing something wrong.

This is an artefact of the imaging by the flycircuit.tw team. Although their images are of high quality (with one of our best ever registration success rates) there must be an uncorrected refractive index mismatch since the brain should be at least 50% larger in Z real life.

> 2. Given a FlyCircuit neuron, I want its distribution across each neuropil region (FCWBNP.surf$RegionList), i.e., the overlapping voxel count of the neuron per neuropil region. This voxel count is provided for 16129 neurons in the dataset http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/flycircuit/dpscanon.rds, but how can I calculate this for a new (not included in the dataset) neuron scraped from the FlyCircuit website?

While the voxel counts would be ideal, I suspect it would also be sufficient for my purposes to instead just get a distribution of the segment lengths (of the neuron) in each neuropil region. Below is the sequence of steps that I have been able to successfully implement so far:
  • fc_read_neurons() - to scrape a neuron from the FlyCircuit website.
  • xform_brain() - to register the neuron into FCWP space.
By default fc_read_neurons transforms neurons into FCWB space so you do not need to do this yourself.
• prune_in_volume() - to obtain a break-up of the number of vertices and segments present in each neuropil region.

I would suggest that you do

resample() e.g. to 1 or 0.5 µm step size to ensure that the neurons are evenly sampled.

For convenience there is a function in a package that was not formally released that should do what you want:

https://github.com/flyconnectome/tracerutils/blob/master/R/synapses_per_neuropil.R#L15

However this will be slow for many neurons. To speed things up, you could do something like the code below which uses some sample data available within nat and the JFRC2 space label field.

All the best,

Greg.

library(nat.flybrains)

# Get label field
# see https://github.com/VirtualFlyBrain/DrosAdultBRAINdomains for details
tf=tempfile(fileext = '.nrrd')
download.file('https://github.com/VirtualFlyBrain/DrosAdultBRAINdomains/blob/master/combinedIndexFiles/JFRCtempate2010.mask130819_Original.nrrd?raw=true', destfile = tf)
labelfield=read.im3d(tf)
# get integer id -> neuropil table
neuropils=read.table('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VirtualFlyBrain/DrosAdultBRAINdomains/master/refData/Original_Index.tsv', sep="\t", header = T)

# Map points to correct space and onto label field using Cell07PNs neuronlist as an example
df=data.frame(neuron=rep(names(Cell07PNs), nvertices(Cell07PNs)))
df=cbind(df, xyzmatrix(Cell07PNs))
# you would use sample = FCWB for your points
dft=xform_brain(df, sample=IS2,ref=JFRC2)
jfrc2indices=coord2ind(xyzmatrix(dft), JFRC2)

# neuropil ids
ids=labelfield[jfrc2indices]
nptable=as.data.frame(table(ids))
merge(nptable, neuropils, by.y="Stack.id", by.x='ids',sort=F)
